text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: High accelerator pool pressure detected in eu-west-1 at 2025-05-03T14:08:08Z — queue depth rising, tail latency > SLO, throttling to 429 increasing

mia_oncall: saw it, joining now. what's the impact?

devon_infra: metrics: queue_length ~ 12k, ready_tokens low, provisioned accelerators at hard limit for this account group (max_pool_shards=16). Autoscaler last scale event at 14:02:03, then hung — logs show leader election succeeded but scale loop errored on DescribeInstances API (403 QuotaExceeded)

anya_prodeng: customers seeing 10-20s generation latency spikes, some request timeouts. CS pinged about two paying customers experiencing degraded throughput.

ops-sre: can we move requests to a fallback model variant with lower memory so we can increase parallelism?

devon_infra: fallback variant (tiny-llama-2) exists but routing policy is set to strict model pin for those orgs — need bypass or emergency override.

mia_oncall: @devon_infra can you apply emergency routing to shift 30% of traffic to fallback? we need to relieve pressure ASAP.
devon_infra: on it. applying temporary routing:
```
routed_override:
  match: org in ["acme-corp","brightpay"]
  percent: 30
  model: tiny-llama-2-v1
  expires: 2025-05-03T15:30:00Z
```

incident-bot: routing override applied by devon_infra at 14:12:09Z

mia_oncall: queue depth dropped to ~9k after override, tail latency down to 6s. still above target but moving.

ryan_support: customer-facing note: sending interim update to affected tenants: "We're seeing degraded generation throughput due to regional accelerator capacity pressure; engineers are applying temporary routing and throttling changes. We'll follow up with ETA for full resolution."

customersuccess-bot: draft ack queued to be sent to customers at 14:20

devon_infra: found root cause candidate: recent rollout (config change at 09:00) toggled continuous batching window and reduced prefix cache TTL from 10m -> 30s. that increased prefix cache misses massively for long-chat workloads, causing more KV-cache rehydration and longer per-request GPU time.

anya_prodeng: that matches the timeline — traffic pattern shifted with a large conversational eval earlier today, cache miss amplification + smaller batch packing = lower effective throughput.

ops-sre: show me the config diff.
devon_infra: diff snippet:
```
- continuous_batching:
-  window_ms: 40
-  max_batch_tokens: 2048
- prefix_cache_ttl: 600
+ continuous_batching:
+  window_ms: 8
+  max_batch_tokens: 1024
+ prefix_cache_ttl: 30
```

mia_oncall: ouch. that explains a lot. who approved that rollout?

devon_infra: rollout was from infra-team/quick-tune at 09:01, PR #4823, approved by infra lead. it was meant to reduce tail latency for short requests but regressed long-chat throughput.

mia_oncall: mitigation plan proposed:
- revert quick-tune rollout (rollback continuous batching window & prefix ttl)
- temporarily raise max_pool_shards for the region (request quota increase) OR enable cross-region spillover
- keep routing override until rollback confirmed
- schedule postmortem and add canary tests for mixed workload cache pressure

ops-sre: I can request quota bump but that's usually slow. cross-region spillover might be fastest — enable eu-central fallback?

devon_infra: enabling cross-region routing now for 15% overflow -> eu-central. toggling spillover flag.

incident-bot: cross-region spillover enabled at 14:24:40Z by devon_infra

mia_oncall: after both routing override + spillover, queue depth is 3k, tail latency ~2.1s, error rate back to baseline. customers patched.

anya_prodeng: rolling back the quick-tune change requires an infra deploy and model-runtime restart on some pools. I'll coordinate a quick rollback patch and target 14:40 deploy window.
devon_infra: rollback PR prepared — tag: revert-quick-tune-4823. planning to deploy to a canary subset first (20% of pools) then full.

ops-sre: please include a config flag to disable continuous batching entirely for the canary so we can compare perf delta.
devon_infra: ack. deploying canary now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started at 14:36:01Z by devon_infra — services: inference-runtime-canary

mia_oncall: monitoring canary metrics... canary queues drop to <200 each, KV cache hit rate back to 82% (from 18%), tokens/sec up 3x. looks good.

devon_infra: promoting rollback to full at 14:42. full deploy started.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: full deploy started at 14:42:22Z by devon_infra — services: inference-runtime

anya_prodeng: full deploy successful at 14:48:33Z — KV cache hit rate across region 79%, queue depth normalized, tail latency stable ~0.85s.

mia_oncall: re-evaluating autoscaler logs — the DescribeInstances 403 was a red herring: the autoscaler crashed earlier due to an unhandled nil panic when handling an empty batch event after window_ms reduction. fix in rollback includes a defensive check.

ops-sre: good catch. add integration test for empty-batch path.

ryan_support: Customer update: "We applied temporary routing and configuration rollback to restore capacity. Performance has returned to normal for most customers; we're investigating the root cause and will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

customersuccess-bot: customer updates sent at 14:55Z

mia_oncall: current status: mitigated, autoscaler healthy, queues normal. Postmortem owner: @anya_prodeng. Action items:
- postmortem (Anya) due EOD+2
- add mixed-workload canaries for prefix-cache TTL and batching window (Devon)
- quota/overflow playbook update (Ops-SRE)
- add PR gate to run synthetic long-chat evals (Product/Devex)

anya_prodeng: taking postmortem. I'll include timeline, config diff, and recommended guardrails.

devon_infra: leaving a follow-up note in infra runbook: avoid reducing prefix_cache_ttl below 5m without eval against long-chat workload.

mia_oncall: handing off to night oncall: @ops-sre you're primary for any regressions — see pinned links to rollback PR and routing override.

ops-sre: ack, I'll monitor and escalate if anything flares. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident closed at 14:59:10Z — severity lowered to P2.
